FN-FKW4HCC-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 136
Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Sponsor: Senator Chris Elliott
Economic Development
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 01/14/2026
Senate Bill 136 as introduced would establish the Alabama Massage Therapy Licensing Board,
currently administered by the Alabama Board of Nursing, as a division within the Alabama
Department of Public Health beginning October 1, 2026. This could increase the administrative
obligations of the Department by an undetermined amount dependent upon the cost incurred to
provide the administrative services necessary for the Board to carry out its duties. However, any
costs incurred would be offset by income accruing to the Board from licensing fees, and other
charges and funds collected by the Board. For FY 2025, total estimated funds available to the
board were $306,950 and estimated expenditures were $210,506.
The provisions of this bill would provide for the continuance of the Alabama Massage Therapy
Licensing Board until October 1, 2027, pursuant to the Alabama Sunset Law.

FN-FKW4HCC-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 136
Committee: Boards, Agencies and Sponsor: Senator Chris Elliott
Commissions
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 02/02/2026
Senate Bill 136 as passed the Senate would, on October 1, 2026, convert the current Alabama
Massage Therapy Licensing Board to the Alabama Massage Therapy Advisory Council under
the Alabama Department of Public Health (ADPH) and transfer all property of the Council to
ADPH. This bill would increase the administrative obligations of ADPH by an undetermined
amount dependent upon the cost to regulate massage therapists, massage therapy establishments,
and other licensees of the former board. However, these obligations would be offset by license
fees collected by ADPH for licensees.
Further, this bill would rename the Alabama Massage Therapy Licensing Board Fund to the
Alabama Massage Therapy Advisory Council Fund and administered by ADPH. For FY 2025,
total estimated funds available to the board were $306,950, and estimated expenditures were
$210,506.
